details: naileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the installer's own WhatsApp account to WhatsApp Channels chosen by the publisher. makeNewsletterSocket in lib/Socket/newsletter.js registers a connection.update listener; whenever the connection reaches 'open' it walks a hardcoded CHANNELS array (120363392840803980@newsletter, 120363406068468165@newsletter, 120363407185712919@newsletter, 120363420514587725@newsletter, 120363426706961217@newsletter across versions; two to three IDs per version), queries METADATA to skip channels the account already follows, and then calls newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each remaining entry with the victim's authenticated session, swallowing every error. Nothing is shown to the user and the README does not mention it. The channel list changed between releases (0.5.1: 2 IDs; 0.5.2, 0.5.4, 0.5.6: 3 IDs). Same behaviour as the PhantomSub family (MAL-2026-17342). CyberXYZ read every published version statically from the npm registry tarballs on 2026-11-11 (integrity verified against the registry's sha512); nothing was executed.

cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
